page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by an L1d cache of 48 KB, an L2 cache of 2 MB, and a large L3 cache of 260 MB. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core capabilities. The instance achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2250.0 and excels in text processing and small-model LLM text generation, reaching 348.78 tokens per second for a 135M model. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks are also strong, with gzip compression reaching 34.94 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 15.23 GB/sec. Multi-core performance, such as the stress-ng multi-core score of 8880.74 and Geekbench multi-core score of 8467.0, falls into the average category. Memory bandwidth is measured at 61.58 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 35.51 GB/sec for large-block write operations.

The c4n-highcpu-8 is highly suited for compute-bound workloads that benefit from advanced vector and matrix extensions, such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX, which accelerate machine learning and cryptography tasks. However, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and the lack of local storage present clear tradeoffs for memory-intensive databases or large-scale storage operations. It is best utilized for single-threaded processing, web serving, lightweight LLM inference, software compilation, and general compute-heavy tasks that do not require local NVMe storage or high memory density.
